newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks seen hitting new 1997 high level.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks seen hitting new 1997 high level.

text.p: Seoul stocks are expected to hit a new 1997 intraday high on Thursday on the back of hopes for an economic turnaround and sharply falling interest rates, brokers said.
But a record level of margin loans would be a hurdle for share prices, they said. Smaller-cap shares account for 60-70 percent of outstanding margin loans.
"The market will be polarised between large-caps and smaller capitalised shares," said Kim Dae-hee of LG Securities.
The composite stock index closed on Wednesday at 738.12, up 14.77 points.
A decision to extend 15.9 billion in rescue loans to Dainong Corp and Midopa Department Store 8000.KS would soothe investors' worries about more corporate financial troubles, brokers said.
"Construction and financial shares, long-time laggards, will benefit from the anticipation of an economic recovery," Kim said.
